posts.title: WINE OF THE WEEK: Château des Jacques Moulin-à-Vent Roches Rouges 2023, Moulin-à-Vent, Beaujolais, France
posts.description: On Beaujolais Nouveau, instead of Nouveau, I’ve got a glass of Château des Jacques Moulin-à-Vent Roches Rouges 2023, a Beaujolais from the most majestic and long-lived of the ten crus (the top individual appellations in Beaujolais). It’s an absolute peach: beautifully perfumed with opulent, dark cherry and red berry fruit. And it's a wine you can enjoy now or put in the cellar

posts.title: WINE OF THE WEEK: Poças Cold Smoked Rosé 2025, Douro, Portugal
posts.description: Most rosé producers are wary of fermenting and/or ageing their wines in new oak. Wine drinkers likewise, I think, are mostly quite wary of the oak-plus-rosé combo. But when it’s done well, as in this Poças Cold Smoked Rosé from Portugal's Douro region, the results can be exciting, giving rosés that go especially well with food and often can also be cellared.

posts.title: WINE OF THE WEEK: Akitu A2 Pinot Noir 2022, Central Otago, New Zealand
posts.description: After last week’s spectacular bargain, this week is a little more indulgent, a cracking New Zealand Pinot Noir that would make an ideal red for the Christmas table, if you can resist it until then, or an ideal present if you can bear to give it away.
